2019_143_121719regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of December 17, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The consent agenda carries prior minutes, a Fifth Third Bank banking resolution, the 2019-2020 Sex Education Advisory Board roster, second reading of ten board policies, the October 2019 Treasurer's Report with its full check register, and the draft Barnard Elementary Emergency Operations Plan; action items add one teacher hire and two business votes. October 2019 total disbursements were $16,653,968.02, and the Board was asked to award Bid Pack #26 at $4,369,839.84 and to adopt a reimbursement resolution tied to not-to-exceed $6,100,000 of 2020 School Building and Site Bonds.

**Meeting** — Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, 7:00 PM, December 17, 2019, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District office 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition** — TSD Mission Moment honoring Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, and Curriculum & Instruction Specialists Jo O'Brien (6-12 ELA) and Lisa McDonald (PreK-5 Literacy) for hosting over 20 districts visiting the district's professional learning model; Kris Griffor to introduce them.

**Consent agenda (items A-G)** — minutes of the November 12, 2019 workshop and the November 19, 2019 meeting; a banking resolution adding signers on the Troy Theater Ensemble account at Fifth Third Bank (established by the late Rick Bodick as sole signer, now under Treasurer Rick West, investments per Board Policy 5000.06 and MCL 380.1223(1)(h)); the 2019-2020 Sex Education Advisory Board, co-chaired by Kristy Pierce and Nicole Jenkins; second reading and adoption of board policies; the October 2019 Treasurer's Report; and the Emergency Operations Plan.

**Policies for adoption (second reading)** — 1000.01 Conflict of Interest; 3000.01 Curriculum Development; 4000.03 Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace; 4000.03 Paid Medical Leave (addition); 4000.03 Medical Examinations; 4000.05 Prohibition of Referral or Assistance; 4000.05 Code of Ethics (addition); 5000.02 Budget Planning and Adoption; 5000.10 Fixed Assets; 7000.11 Volunteers (addition). Drafted by Lusk and Albertson and reviewed by the Policy Committee on October 23, 2019. Policy 5000.02 keeps the pledge to maintain a minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent; Policy 5000.10 sets a $5,000 capitalization threshold; Policy 7000.11 requires ICHAT criminal background checks for every volunteer.

**General Fund statement, July 1 - October 31, 2019** (budget approved 6/11/19): total revenues $157,288,640 budget, $29,000,721 actual, 18.44%, $128,287,919 available; total expenditures $158,261,349 budget, $30,179,070 actual, 19.07%, $128,082,279 available; revenues over (under) expenditures ($972,709) budgeted and ($1,178,349) actual. Instruction posted $17,500,884 of $106,846,362 (16.38%); support services $12,641,138 of $51,191,443 (24.69%).

**Barnard Elementary Emergency Operations Plan (DRAFT 12/16/19)** — marked For Official Use Only and exempt under Section 13(1)(y) of the Michigan FOIA, Act 442 of 1976; authority MCL 380.1308b and district Policy 6000.03. Population: 488 students, 1 administrator, 2 office/support staff, 42 teachers/specialists, 12 instructional assistants, 9 cafeteria staff, 3 maintenance/custodial staff, 5 bus drivers. Uses the ALICE protocol and the RAVE Panic Button app; principal Melanie Morey; alternate sites are the Boys and Girls Club of Troy and Big Beaver United Methodist Church, both 0.9 miles away on John R Rd.

**Personnel** — probationary contract for Megan Murray, 1.0 Special Education ASD Room Teacher, Leonard Elementary, for 2019-2020.

**Business** — Bid Pack #26 (RFP 9894) awards totaling $4,046,148.00 plus $323,691.84 contingency for a $4,369,839.84 total, funded from the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds and the Sinking Fund; and a reimbursement resolution letting the General Fund be repaid from proceeds of the 2020 School Building and Site Bonds, capped at $6,100,000.

Board of Education regular meeting packet, Troy School District (4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us), for the meeting of December 17, 2019 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Consent agenda items A-G (p. 4) precede Personnel (p. 288) and Business (pp. 290, 294). The TSD Mission Moment recognizes Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, and Curriculum & Instruction Specialists Jo O'Brien (6-12 English Language Arts) and Lisa McDonald (PreK-5 Literacy) for hosting over 20 different districts visiting the professional learning model; Kris Griffor introduces them.

**Prior minutes.** The November 12, 2019 workshop at the Administration Building opened at 6:00 p.m. under President Schmidt with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, plus Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Harris, Carson and West, and leadership coach David Hulings; adjourned 9:53 p.m. The November 19, 2019 regular meeting began 7:00 p.m. with Mrs. Hammond absent, recognizing Athens Photography 2 students and the Athens boys' soccer MHSAA Division One state champions under coach Todd Heugh. Resolution 19-092 approved consent items A-H (Yes 6, No 0); Resolution 19-093 named Jordan Harris chief spokesperson with Rick West, Christine DiPilato, Kris Griffor, Kandice Moynihan, Jessica Carrier and John Pagel for TEA/MEA/NEA negotiations on a contract expiring January 31, 2020; Resolution 19-094 awarded roofing from the 2019 Capital Projects Fund - JD Candler $1,469,500.00, Royal West $740,000.00 for Troy High, contingency $110,475.00, total $2,319,975.00. Dr. Machesky cited Boulan Park Middle School, Martell Elementary and Wass Elementary as National Blue Ribbon Schools. Adjourned 8:02 p.m., Secretary Gary N. Hauff.

**Banking resolution.** Adds signers on the Troy Theater Ensemble account for Troy High School at Fifth Third Bank, opened by the late Rick Bodick as sole signer. Treasurer Rick West is directed to deposit public monies there; checks may carry his facsimile signature, or in emergencies the handwritten signature of Rick West or Superintendent Richard M. Machesky. Investments follow Board Policy 5000.06 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code; certified this 17th day of December 2019, Oakland County, Michigan.

**Sex Education Advisory Board 2019-2020** (roster updated 12/17/19), co-chaired by Kristy Pierce (AP, Boulan Park Middle School) and resident Nicole Jenkins, with Ann O'Neill, Lisa Danhoff, Andrea Lothian and Kevin Wilson; Rev. Gregg Mayberry of Big Beaver United Methodist Church; David Roth of the Oakland Health Department; parents Kelly Jones, Harleen Singh, Patti Stark, Cherie Armstrong and Randy Maddock; and students Katie Austin and Noah Scudder.

**Board policies, second reading and adoption.** Ten items: 1000.01 Conflict of Interest; 3000.01 Curriculum Development (per MCL 380.1282(2)); 4000.03 Alcohol and Drug-Free Workplace (federal Drug-Free Workplace Act, 41 USC 8101 et seq.; written notice no more than three business days after arraignment; marijuana barred on school grounds); 4000.03 Paid Medical Leave (addition under the Michigan Paid Medical Leave Act, MCL 408.961 et seq., enacted December 2018); 4000.03 Medical Examinations (costs borne by the district); 4000.05 Prohibition of Referral or Assistance (House Bill 4242 amending MCL 388.1766 - districts no longer forfeit $100,000 in state aid but may forfeit 1% of state aid funding, with personnel fines of no less than 3% of annual compensation, and compliance with MCL 380.1507); 4000.05 Code of Ethics (addition adopting the MDE-approved Michigan Code of Educational Ethics); 5000.02 Budget Planning and Adoption (GASB Statement No. 54 superseded by GASB 84; adoption prior to July 1; minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent); 5000.10 Fixed Assets (items over $5,000 with useful life over one year, or under $5,000 if theft prone); and 7000.11 Volunteers (ICHAT check for every volunteer; convictions listed under MCL 380.1535a or MCL 380.1539b disqualify). Memo from Rick West to Dr. Rich Machesky dated November 7, 2019; the Policy Committee reviewed Lusk and Albertson updates October 23, 2019; first reading November 19, 2019.

**Treasurer's Report, October 2019.** Transmitted by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services (248-823-4022), dated December 17, 2019. **Barnard Elementary Emergency Operations Plan, DRAFT 12/16/19.** Marked For Official Use Only and exempt from disclosure under Section 13(1)(y) of the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act 442 of 1976; point of contact Dr. Richard Machesky. Signature blocks list Machesky, Board President Karl Schmidt, the building principal, Troy Police Chief Frank Nastasi, Troy Fire Chief David Roberts, City of Troy Emergency Management Specialist Kristin Dayag, and Oakland County Emergency Manager Thomas Hardesty. Building population: 488 students, 1 administrator, 2 office/support staff, 42 teachers/specialists, 12 instructional assistants, 9 cafeteria staff, 3 maintenance/custodial staff, 5 bus drivers. Translation services are listed for Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada and Tamil. The plan cites the ALICE protocol (Alert, Lockdown, Inform, Counter, Evacuate), the RAVE Panic Button/Staff Assist app, the School Messenger System, PowerSchool rosters, and FEMA guidance that schools may have to be self-sustaining for up to 72 hours; authorities are MCL 380.1308b and district Policy 6000.03 School Crisis, Response and Closure. Principal Melanie Morey leads the Crisis Response Team; alternate locations are the Boys and Girls Club of Troy, 3670 John R Rd. (0.9 miles, Jim Adams) and Big Beaver United Methodist Church, 3753 John R Rd. (0.9 miles, Pastor Gregg Mayberry). Oakland County Emergency Management agrees to supply a Medical Point of Distribution at Troy High School.

**Personnel.** A probationary contract for 2019-2020 for Megan Murray, 1.0 Special Education ASD Room Teacher at Leonard Elementary; M.S. in Educational Leadership, Fort Hays State University, May 2016; B.S., Mild/Moderate Intervention Specialist K-12, Bowling Green State University, May 2013; Professional Teaching Certificate November 2019; prior service in Augusta, Georgia, Wamego, Kansas, and Spring Lake, North Carolina.

**Bid Pack #26.** RFP 9894 covers mechanical/electrical upgrades and window/door replacements at Hill and Wattles Elementary, ADA stage renovations at Costello, Martell and IAE, and pool and art room work at Athens High School; proposals were received November 1, 2019 and reviewed by TSD Operations, TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates, Barton Malow and Michelle Kerns. Memo from Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance & Operations (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083), to Rick West dated November 25, 2019, with a Barton Malow letter of the same date from Project Manager Christa Amalio. Awards: R & E Development, General Trades, $698,155.00; Hewett Company, Exterior Doors/Windows, $1,036,050.00; Seven Brothers Painting, $50,743.00; Contrast Mechanical, $1,111,000.00; Air Solutions, Test & Balance, $23,500.00; MCMI, Temperature Controls, $337,700.00; Great Lakes Power & Lighting, Electrical, $789,000.00; total contract awards $4,046,148.00, contingency of 8% at $323,691.84, total $4,369,839.84, funded from the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds and the Sinking Fund. Swimming pool equipment and scaffolding drew too few bids and will be rebid in December 2019 for award in January 2020.

**2020 School Building and Site Bonds.** A reimbursement resolution under Treas. Reg. Sec. 1.150-2 preserving the district's ability to reimburse its General Fund from bond proceeds for acquiring real property and a building and renovating, equipping and furnishing it. The Board authorized bonds not to exceed $6,100,000 on September 17, 2019; reimbursement covers expenditures made after sixty (60) days prior to the resolution, allocated no later than 18 months after payment or placed-in-service and never more than three (3) years after the original expenditure. Certified by Gary Hauff, Secretary, under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.
